original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: All-length no-saving for every type in an arbitrary even orthogonal binary basis, including coordinate old calls, plus one fresh pairing-one bridge at the actual pattern relation budget.
scope_change_reason: Replace the extremal edge-pair geometry by an arbitrary old basis. Use its Boolean diagonal kernel and the actual conjugated endpoint algebra; include the subextremal no-edge seven-core.
bottleneck_link: Exclude a larger specified scalar word class, including the remaining no-edge seven-image family, before native construction or broader searches.
stop_rule: Stop at the arbitrary-basis one-bridge theorem and exact target invoice. Extra types, omitted types and larger relation budgets remain separate.
evidence: PROOF.md; RESULT.json; all 20166 GL2/GL4 bases, 130320 degree-two orders, 20880 full Laurent words, eight full ambient fixtures and quotient/idempotence controls.

open_questions.question: Can a specified second nonorthogonal bridge or larger relation budget support a legal saving?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The one-bridge alphabet cannot save rank at the stated budget, but other alphabets are not excluded.
open_questions.first_step: State the full alphabet and paid/target invoice; do not treat failure of a one-bridge hypothesis as a saving.
open_questions.blocked_by: No saving word or native interface is supplied.

family_decision.decision: Change the exact word alphabet from disjoint edge pairs to an arbitrary even old orthogonal basis, then stop at the resulting negative theorem.
family_decision.evidence_status: Author-checked all-width/all-length proof, exact finite corroboration, and explicit source-dependent no-edge corollary.
family_decision.boundary: All old types in one even orthogonal binary basis plus one fixed fresh bridge; paid-generated torsion-free abelian group; relation rank at most actual pattern dimension; full diagonal monomial endpoint.
family_decision.alternative: A blind word search in the remaining no-edge seven-core would not establish arbitrary length or arbitrary old-basis coverage.
family_decision.construction_gate: No new native construction is proposed. A future saving needs a different stated alphabet or budget and a complete invoice.
